_doc: South America past the gringo trail — the second cities and offshore islands of Brazil, the Peruvian north, Colombia's Caribbean edge, and the wildlife country at both ends of the continent.

destinations.name: São Paulo
destinations.blurb: South America's restless giant — the continent's best restaurant scene, MASP's collection floating on red concrete, Japanese Liberdade and Italian Bixiga, and a nightlife that genuinely does not stop.

destinations.name: Fernando de Noronha
destinations.blurb: A volcanic archipelago 350km offshore that caps visitor numbers and charges you to arrive — the result is Baía do Sancho, regularly voted the best beach on earth, and spinner dolphins in their hundreds at dawn.
photos: Baia do Sancho Fernando de Noronha

destinations.name: Recife & Olinda
destinations.blurb: Bridges and canals gave Recife its Venice-of-Brazil nickname, but the real draw is Olinda on the hill above — painted colonial streets and the frevo carnival that is the loudest, least touristed in the country.

destinations.name: Ouro Preto & Minas
destinations.blurb: Brazil's gold-rush baroque, preserved whole — cobbled streets falling down hillsides between blue and white churches carved by Aleijadinho, and a Minas kitchen that is the country's most loved regional cooking.
photos: Sao Francisco de Assis Ouro Preto

destinations.name: Ilha Grande
destinations.blurb: A former prison island turned car-free national park three hours from Rio — you walk everywhere, the Atlantic forest comes down to the sand, and Lopes Mendes is a two-hour hike that pays you back in full.

destinations.name: Lake Titicaca & Puno
destinations.blurb: The highest navigable lake in the world, its light almost painful at 3,800m — floating reed islands of the Uros, the weaving island of Taquile, and Sillustani's funeral towers on the plain above.

destinations.name: Nazca & Paracas
destinations.blurb: Lines drawn across the desert two thousand years ago and legible only from the air, and up the coast the Paracas reserve and Ballestas islands — sea lions, penguins and guano cliffs, plus the dune oasis at Huacachina.

destinations.name: Chachapoyas & Kuélap
destinations.blurb: A walled citadel older than Machu Picchu on a cloud-forest ridge, reached now by cable car — plus Gocta, one of the world's tallest waterfalls, and sarcophagi standing in cliff niches above the valley.

destinations.name: Máncora
destinations.blurb: Peru's warm-water exception — a left-hand point break that runs for hundreds of metres, ceviche eaten barefoot, and whale watching from July when the humpbacks come north to calve.

destinations.name: San Andrés & Providencia
destinations.blurb: Colombia's Caribbean islands, 700km off its own coast and closer to Nicaragua — Creole-speaking, reggae-playing, and ringed by the sea of seven colours over the third-largest barrier reef in the world.
photos: San Andres sea of seven colours

destinations.name: La Guajira
destinations.blurb: The continent's northern tip, where desert runs straight into the Caribbean — Wayuu rancherías, dunes at Taroa you slide down into the sea, and the lighthouse at Punta Gallinas with nothing beyond it.

destinations.name: Villa de Leyva & Boyacá
destinations.blurb: One of the largest cobbled plazas in the Americas, whitewashed and almost unchanged since the 1570s — with fossil beds, an emerald-green desert and the Iguaque lakes an easy ride into the hills behind.

destinations.name: Península Valdés
destinations.blurb: Southern right whales calving close enough to the shore at Puerto Pirámides that you can watch from a cliff — plus orcas that beach themselves deliberately to take sea lion pups at Punta Norte.

destinations.name: Esteros del Iberá
destinations.blurb: The Pantanal's quieter Argentine cousin — floating islands and lagoons where capybara and caiman ignore you at arm's length, and where jaguar, giant otter and macaw have all been reintroduced.

destinations.name: The Elqui Valley
destinations.blurb: A narrow green valley cut into brown desert hills, planted with the muscat that becomes pisco — and above it, skies so reliably clear that the world's observatories queue up for space on the ridgelines.

destinations.name: The Carretera Austral
destinations.blurb: 1,200km of mostly gravel through Chilean Patagonia, ferry-hopping between fjords — the marble caves at General Carrera, hanging glaciers at Queulat, and Patagonia National Park at the far end.

destinations.name: Cuenca
destinations.blurb: Ecuador's most graceful colonial city, blue-domed and set on four rivers at 2,500m — the place Panama hats are actually made, with the páramo lakes of Cajas half an hour up the road.

destinations.name: Montevideo & Colonia
destinations.blurb: A capital with a 22km rambla along the river-sea, the continent's longest carnival and a candombe drum-line that comes down the street on Sunday nights — plus cobbled Colonia, a ferry ride from Buenos Aires.

destinations.name: Madidi & Rurrenabaque
destinations.blurb: Where the Andes fall into the Amazon, and the biodiversity count goes off the scale — community-run lodges upriver in Madidi, and pampas trips where pink river dolphins surface beside the boat.
